title: Minimum Window Substring
summary: Find the shortest piece of a string that contains every character of another string, repeats included.
validate: (result, args, expected) => { const [s, t] = args; if (typeof result !== "string") return "Return a string."; if (expected === "") return result === "" ? true : "No window of s contains every character of t, so the answer is \"\"."; if (result.length !== expected.length) return "The shortest valid window has length " + expected.length + ", but yours has length " + result.length + "."; if (!s.includes(result)) return "Your answer is not a substring of s."; const need = {}; for (const c of t) need[c] = (need[c] || 0) + 1; for (const c of result) if (need[c]) need[c]--; return Object.values(need).every((v) => v === 0) ? true : "Your window is missing some characters of t (repeats count)."; }

tests.explain: "CAB" (indices 5 to 7) contains A, B and C, and no window of 3 characters elsewhere does.
t needs two c's but s has only one, so no window works: return "".
Letters are case-sensitive: the window must contain a lowercase a and a lowercase b, so the shortest is "aBb".

hints: Count what t needs: a map from character to how many copies are required.
Extend a window to the right, and keep one number, missing, for how many required characters are still not covered. The window is valid when missing is 0.
While the window is valid, record it if it is the shortest so far, then move left forward. When removing a character makes missing positive again, go back to extending right.

complexity.time: O(m + n): each index of s enters and leaves the window once, plus counting t
complexity.space: O(k): counts for the distinct characters of t
